example: Touching a hot surface changes the environment. Neurons detect that stimulus, communicate the change through a circuit, and command muscles to withdraw the hand.

en.title: From Stimulus to Response
en.learning_objective: Trace how cooperating neurons turn an environmental change into a body response.
en.simple_explanation: A stimulus is a detectable change, such as heat touching the skin. According to the source, neurons sense environmental changes, communicate those changes to other neurons, and command the body's responses.
en.how_it_works: The process depends on specialized cells working together. One neuron detects the change. Communication passes information among neurons. Other neurons then issue an output that produces a response. Glia support, nourish, and insulate the neurons that perform this information processing.
en.visual:
stimulus: heat
↓ detected by neurons
↓ communicated through neurons
command → muscle response
en.use_case: When you touch a hot surface, predict the causal order before drawing the circuit: heat first, neural detection and communication next, then a command that moves the hand away.
en.expected_result: Your trace begins with the environmental change and ends with an observable body action.
en.what_to_notice: The response is not produced by one isolated cell. Specialized neurons must detect, relay, and command in an ordered circuit, while glia support their operation.
en.common_mistake: Do not draw the muscle response before neural communication or treat glia as the cells carrying most information processing.
en.practical_tip: Label every arrow with an action—detects, communicates, or commands—so the diagram shows causation rather than a list of parts.
en.question: What three neuronal functions connect an environmental stimulus to a body response?
en.answer: Neurons sense the change, communicate it to other neurons, and command the response.

review_items.question: What causal sequence turns a stimulus into a response?
review_items.answer: Stimulus detection → communication among neurons → command → body response.

review_items.question: Why must neurons communicate after one detects a stimulus?
review_items.answer: Detection identifies the change; communication carries that information so other neurons can issue a coordinated command.

review_items.question: A hand withdraws after touching heat. What belongs at the start and end of the trace?
review_items.answer: Start with heat as the stimulus; end with the commanded muscle withdrawal.

active_exercise.instruction: Draw a four-stage causal diagram for touching a hot surface: stimulus, neuronal detection, communication between neurons, and command to a muscle. Annotate each arrow with what changes, and mark glia beside the neural stages as support rather than the signal path.
active_exercise.output: Save one labeled causal diagram titled `stimulus-to-response`.
